1770.title: --base-branch resolves against the stale local ref, so spawned worktrees silently start behind
1770.rootCauseOneLine: A plain --base-branch name is passed verbatim to the daemon, where createWorktree only fetches remote-qualified names (resolveRemoteBaseBranch returns null for names without a remote prefix) and the server's smart origin-vs-local resolution runs only for the {kind:"default"} spec, so `git worktree add … main` resolves the unfetched local refs/heads/main.
1770.proposedFix: Server-side: stop returning early for named specs in resolveManagedDefaultBaseBranchForCreate (apps/server/src/services/threads/thread-create.ts) and, when the named branch is the checkout's default branch, apply resolveDefaultWorktreeBaseBranch after host.list_branches (which already fetches) so equal/local-behind resolves to origin/<name> while ahead/diverged keeps local; optionally extend host.list_branches to report the relation for an arbitrary selectedBranch (protocol bump). Alternatively/additionally in the daemon (packages/host-workspace/src/provisioning.ts createWorktree): for a plain-name base, fetch its upstream, compare with rev-list --left-right --count, prefer upstream when local is behind-only, emit transcript steps stating the resolved base commit and relation, degrade fetch failure to a warning; gate the behaviour so thread forks (which intentionally use the source env's local branch) are unaffected. Also print the resolved base commit in `bb thread spawn`/`bb environment show`, and document in docs/worktrees.md, the CLI help, and bb-guide-threads.md exactly which ref a bare name resolves to. Add regression tests: local main behind (expect fetch + fresh HEAD), local main ahead/diverged (stay local), origin/main (existing).
1770.caveats: Worktree was handed to me at a108fa7ef (origin/main); I checked out 16ceb3a54 detached before the live repro, and none of the intervening commits touch the relevant files. Bug is not visual; screenshots show the app's provisioning transcript for evidence only. Reporter's fleet numbers (7/12 checkouts behind, 65-commit anecdote) are unverifiable. Each live spawn used one tiny codex turn.

1762.title: browser_screenshot returns the string "OK" and no image; the PNG is captured then dropped

1762.proposedFix: Make decodeToolCallResponsePayload return { content, images: {data,mimeType}[], isError } by parsing data: URLs from inputImage items (fall back to "OK" only when there is neither text nor image); thread the optional images through the bridge ToolCallResult / pending-tool-call tracker; emit native image parts in the claude-code MCP proxy (tool-proxy-mcp.ts), the pi tool proxy (agent-runtime pi/bridge/tool-proxy.ts) and the ACP bridge->MCP shim (extend its socket schema). Codex needs no change. Validated locally: repro tests pass, claude-code and pi live threads answer "IMAGE red"; diff at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1762/repro/proposed-fix.diff (one ACP test asserts the exact result shape and needs images: [] added). No HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed (server<->daemon wire unchanged).

The two "adjacent CLI bugs" (--help treated as path, ./screenshot.png relative to server cwd) are plugin bugs: bb forwards argv verbatim and cwd in PluginCliContext, and the plugin ignores ctx.cwd. Bug still present on origin/main a108fa7ef (#1742 refactor kept the same decoder). Worktree left with the candidate fix applied plus two repro test files (uncommitted). Live repro used real claude-code/codex/pi turns on the dev instance (5 tiny prompts).

1758.title: github plugin latches needs-configuration on one transient gh auth failure and never re-probes
1758.rootCauseOneLine: plugins/github/server.ts checkAuth() maps every `gh auth status` failure (a network probe: outage, locked keychain, 10 s timeout) to NeedsConfigurationError, which the load-time probe reports via bb.status.needsConfiguration and the sync service throws out of start(); the plugin runtime then stops the service "until reload" and keeps needs-configuration until the next load, the plugin API has no way to clear it, and the app skips the frontend bundle of non-running plugins, so nothing ever re-runs gh and the "run gh auth login" hint cannot help.
1758.proposedFix: Plugin-only change in plugins/github/server.ts (prototype diff at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1758/repro/proposed-fix.diff, applied in the worktree; makes the 4-test repro file pass and keeps bb-plugin-github typecheck/tests green): (1) checkAuth() throws NeedsConfigurationError only when gh is missing or holds no credentials at all, using the network-free `gh auth token` to tell "not logged in" from "logged in but the API probe failed"; other failures become a plain Error carrying gh's stderr. (2) The sync service catches non-configuration errors inside its loop and retries with backoff (30 s doubling to the 5-min interval) instead of throwing out of start(). (3) The status RPC re-runs checkAuth() when the last probe failed so the panel/CLI reflect current state. (4) Load-time only calls bb.status.needsConfiguration for the two genuine configuration cases and logs transient failures. Follow-ups: reword the panel banner in app.tsx, make resolveGh() distinguish ENOENT from timeout, and optionally add an experimental_ degraded/clear status API to the plugin runtime so bb plugin list can show a transient gh problem.
1758.caveats: Reproduced on Linux with gh 2.96.0 (issue reports macOS 26 / gh 2.95.0 / bb 0.38.0); the macOS locked-keychain trigger is unverified here but takes the identical code path (any non-zero exit of `gh auth status`). Live repro used a shim that runs the real gh through a dead proxy (HTTPS_PROXY to a closed port) to simulate the network outage; the first live attempt was confounded by the dev server hot-reloading the plugin when the test file was created under plugins/github (documented in 02-plugin-list-after-gh-online.txt) and was redone cleanly. The worktree is left with the prototype fix applied to plugins/github/server.ts and the new test file plugins/github/server.auth-latch.test.ts (uncommitted). Dev instance stopped.

1749.title: timelineWindowEventBudget assumes 0.06ms/event; measured 0.479ms/event on a 4-core host
1749.rootCauseOneLine: timelineWindowEventBudget bounds synchronous timeline builds by a fixed event count justified by a one-host "0.06ms/event" figure, but build cost is CPU- and payload-byte-dependent (SQLite read + JSON.parse ~80%), so on slow hosts a full 1500-event window blocks the event loop far longer than the ~100ms the constant promises; the existing 4 MiB byte cut is not operator-tunable and never engages for latency.

prReviews.topFinding: Docs-only; bakes one VPS's unverifiable and selection-biased numbers (derived only from >=150ms slow-build log lines) into the shared feature-flags.ts JSDoc, and the configuration.md recipe omits that the log samples only the slow tail and that a whole finished turn is always returned even above the budget; does not touch the real lever (the existing byte-based window cut).

1749.proposedFix: Promote the existing THREAD_TIMELINE_EVENT_DATA_BYTE_LIMIT (4 MiB, applyTimelineWindowByteBudget / findStoredTimelineWindowByteBudgetFloor) to a feature flag timelineWindowByteBudget (BB_FF_TIMELINE_WINDOW_BYTE_BUDGET) threaded like eventBudget, default ~1.5 MiB with 4 MiB kept as the memory clamp; document both knobs (configuration.md, guide template, bb-cli skill) and reword the source comment to say the count is a hardware/payload-dependent proxy. Avoid runtime calibration unless the timeline cache and latest-rows keys also include the effective budget. Structural fix (out of scope): incremental projection or moving the build off the event loop.
1749.caveats: Revision: fixed the major finding — the "rebuilds continuously / per appended event" claim is now marked Verified (cache key) / Partially (rebuild rate), citing the client-side trailing-refetch pacing in realtime-cache-registry.ts#L135-L157 (min 50ms, max 1s, ~50% duty cycle, from PR #882); root-cause paragraph reworded to sustained-but-coalesced rebuilds. Minors: renamed the informational test scenario (repro file + inline listing), credited PR #882's "Known limits" (count-not-bytes, "1500 is a first guess"), and the contended step now states the Linux/taskset prerequisite, the ~0.067 ms/event trip threshold and host dependence; run-contended.sh gained a taskset check and LOOPS override (default 3 unchanged). Re-ran both after the changes at 16ceb3a54: idle 2 passed (budget=1500 p50=32.3ms, 0.022 ms/evt); contended 1 failed, expected 186.4 <= 100 (verifier saw 141.9, original 124.5) — same assertion, magnitude varies with host load. Still could not measure on the reporter's 4-core VPS; hardware dependence demonstrated by CPU throttling only. Reporter's 0.479 ms/event is a slow-tail estimate (log fires only for builds >= 150ms). Nothing on origin/main after base changes this code. No dev instance or provider turns needed.

1748.title: Server heap is sized from host RAM, not the cgroup limit, so it fills the memory cap with garbage
1748.rootCauseOneLine: Node already sizes the V8 heap from min(RAM, cgroup memory.max/memory.high) via uv_get_constrained_memory; the reporter's 1728 MB is exactly the value derived from MemoryHigh=3G (a 4.9 GiB host with no cgroup gives 2240 MB), so the "cgroup ignored" premise is false; the residual real gap is that every co-located Node process (server, daemon, bridges) gets ~half the cgroup and there is no per-process heap knob because NODE_OPTIONS is inherited by all of them.

prReviews.topFinding: resolveServerNodeFlags reads process.env, so `bb-app env set BB_SERVER_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB` (which the PR's docs row advertises) is silently ignored (verified live: server spawned without the flag while its env has the value); also the validation error is swallowed by `bb-app start` and reported as 'health check timed out', and the docs/comment restate the false 'Node ignores cgroup limits' premise.

1748.proposedFix: Do not implement the issue as filed (deriving --max-old-space-size from memory.max re-implements Node's default and yields the same 1728 MB); retitle to the real gap: no way to cap the server heap independently of daemon/bridges in a shared cgroup. If a knob is wanted, read it from the launcher's resolved env (runtime.serverEnv), validate at option-resolution time so bb-app start surfaces the error, apply at both server spawn sites, document without the wrong premise, add tests. Optionally a co-location-aware default (server gets ~40% of min(memory.high, memory.max) when a cgroup limit is detected, overridable), and separately heap-snapshot the server's ~625 MB trough to see whether it is retained live state.
1748.caveats: Reporter's RSS/OOM measurements are host-specific and unverifiable here; NODE_OPTIONS propagation to bridge processes was verified by code and the existing process-utils unit test, not by spawning a live provider turn; the native claude binary on this machine ignores NODE_OPTIONS (npm/Node installs would not). One `bb-app env set` invocation during PR testing lacked BB_SERVER_PORT and triggered a harmless config reload on the machine's real bb server on :38886 (no data changed). Test cgroup runs used systemd-run --user --scope on this host's node 24.18 (reporter has 24.19; same libuv/Node logic).

1721.title: pi `/compact` on a small session surfaces as a failed turn and puts the thread in error state
1721.rootCauseOneLine: Pi emits compaction_end{reason:"manual", errorMessage:"Compaction failed: Nothing to compact (session too small)"} for a benign refusal, and bb's pi translator (packages/agent-runtime/src/pi/event-translation.ts compaction_end branch) maps every manual compaction_end with an errorMessage to turn/completed status=failed, which the server turns into run.failed -> thread status error (and steer-mode `bb thread tell` then 409s with "Thread is not active").
1721.proposedFix: In packages/agent-runtime/src/pi/event-translation.ts (compaction_end, reason=manual, !aborted): classify pi's pre-flight refusals ("Compaction failed: Nothing to compact (session too small)" and "Compaction failed: Already compacted") as a no-op and emit turn/completed status=completed (no error) so the server applies run.succeeded -> idle; keep status=failed for real failures (e.g. "Summarization failed: ..."). Close the pending contextCompaction row truthfully: cheapest is to also emit provider/error{message:"Context compaction skipped", detail:<pi message>} (server lifecycle ignores provider/error; thread-view already finalizes the row from it — retitle in packages/thread-view/src/operation-projection.ts finalizeOpenCompactionsForTurn when the turn completed), or add a skipped/detail field to the contextCompaction item + item/completed (domain change, needs HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump). Update the pinned test event-translation.test.ts:432-465 which currently uses the "Nothing to compact" message as its failure example, and add the no-op case (repro test provided). Optional: server compact route could pre-empt with a friendly 409 based on contextWindowUsage, but keepRecentTokens is pi-side so not the primary fix.
1721.caveats: Live repro used pi model openai-codex/gpt-5.4-mini at ~6.4k tokens; the issue's 4.8k/22.4k observations and the >34k success path were not re-run (consistent with code and existing tests). The 409 on `bb thread tell` is steer-mode specific (generic for any error-state thread); a start-mode send recovers the thread. Text-matching pi's error strings is brittle across pi upgrades (pinned at pi-coding-agent 0.84.0). Worktree HEAD was initially a108fa7ef (5 commits past base); I checked out 16ceb3a54 for the repro; origin/main does not fix it. Repro test file left uncommitted in the worktree at packages/agent-runtime/src/pi/issue-1721-compact-too-small.test.ts.

1718.title: claude-code: user message sent after stopping a thread with backgrounded work is dropped
1718.rootCauseOneLine: On resume after a process died with a background shell task alive, Claude Code CLI 2.1.234 emits a zero-work `result` (num_turns 0, origin.kind=task-notification) before processing the new prompt, and bb's claude-code translator (resolveProviderTerminalTurn, added by #1432) settles the pending user message on it, producing an empty turn and pushing the real answer into an unsolicited turn.
1718.proposedFix: In plugins/provider-claude-code/src/event-translation.ts `case "result"`, do not call resolveProviderTerminalTurn (which opens a turn for pending accepted user input) when the SDK result carries origin.kind === "task-notification"; use state.currentTurnId only (so a live-session notification loop that already opened a turn still completes). Add `origin` to claudeResultMessageSchema in schemas.ts. Diff at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1718/repro/1718-proposed-fix.diff; verified with the two new repro tests, the full plugin suite (263 pass) + typecheck, and an end-to-end rerun where the user's turn correctly owns input/accepted, the answer and turn/completed. No daemon protocol change.
1718.caveats: The reporter's third bullet (unsolicited turn answered the previous question) was not reproduced as such: in all runs the model answered the new prompt; it is plausible model behaviour given the synthesized "stopped" notification in context, and does not change the mechanism. Pre-#1432 behaviour was inferred from the #1432 diff (old guard `if (state.currentTurnId)`), not re-run. The date the CLI started emitting the orphaned-task settlement is unknown; it exists in CLI 2.1.234 / SDK 0.3.197. A related live-session race (task-notification loop draining a concurrently accepted prompt) remains after the proposed fix. The worktree was reset to 16ceb3a54 (branch issue-1718-base) for the repro; source changes were reverted and only the diff was kept.

1712.title: Claude Plan mode can skip the proposal flow in a mid-conversation thread
1712.rootCauseOneLine: Since #1640 the bridge-protocol adapter always classifies option changes as "live" (no thread/resume), and the Claude bridge's turn/start|steer path only uses providerOptions.claudeCodePermissionMode to strip the "/plan" mention — it never calls setPermissionMode("plan") on the live SDK session, so a mid-conversation /plan runs in the user's normal preset and Claude executes the task instead of planning/proposing via ExitPlanMode.
1712.proposedFix: In plugins/provider-claude-code: (1) session-params.ts buildClaudeTurnParams forwards providerOptions.claudeCodePermissionMode; (2) bridge/commands.ts claudeTurnStartParamsSchema/claudeTurnSteerParamsSchema gain claudeCodePermissionMode: z.literal("plan").optional(); (3) bridge/bridge.ts adds enterPlanModeIfRequested() which, when the turn requests plan and threadSession.permissionMode !== "plan", sets threadSession.permissionMode = "plan" and awaits threadSession.session.setPermissionMode("plan"), called right after applyLiveSessionSettings in runTurnStart and runTurnSteer before the prompt is queued. approvedPlanPermissionMode is untouched so #1260's approval restore still works. No HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed (canonical wire already carries the knob). Verified: repro bridge test fails on base (setPermissionMode called 0 times) and passes with the fix; all 262 plugin tests pass; live mid-thread /plan now yields plan file -> ExitPlanMode -> pending plan approval -> approve completes.
1712.caveats: The reporter ran 0.37.0, which predates #1640; at that version a mid-thread /plan DID rebuild the session in plan mode via thread/resume (consistent with the reported plan-file link), and the missing ExitPlanMode there is most likely model behavior (ExitPlanMode is a deferred tool needing a ToolSearch lookup first, seen in every successful run) — not reproduced deterministically, so confidence about the 0.37.0 mechanism is medium. On main the failure is worse and deterministic (no plan mode at all). The worktree started at a108fa7ef (origin/main) rather than 16ceb3a54; I checked out 16ceb3a54 for all repro work; the 5 intervening commits do not touch plan mode. CLI `bb thread tell` cannot express a /plan mention (mentions: []), so the repro posts the app composer's structured input via the send API. The worktree is left with the fix + test applied (uncommitted).

1711.title: Cross-project child thread creation rejects a valid parent thread
1711.rootCauseOneLine: assertValidParentThread (apps/server/src/services/threads/thread-parent.ts:161-163) deliberately rejects any parent whose projectId differs from the new thread's with 400 parent_thread_invalid reason=wrong_project; the CLI hides the reason, and isLiveParentThread duplicates the same-project assumption for the parent permission ceiling and env inheritance.
1711.proposedFix: If cross-project parents are wanted: drop the wrong_project branch in assertValidParentThread; split isLiveParentThread so the project comparison remains only where the parent's environment is reused (personal-project branch of resolveCreateThreadEnvironment) while the permission ceiling (#1593), visibility inheritance and managed-child semantics apply regardless of project (add a test that an auto parent's cross-project child requesting full is clamped); remove "wrong_project" from ParentThreadInvalidReason in server-contract + app lifecycle-errors mapping (as PR #235 did for the sender variant); make the sidebar (projectThreadGroups.ts) and the parent's child-list query (ThreadDetailView useProjectThreadSubset) project-agnostic and add a project indicator; update bb-guide-threads.md/bb-cli skill. Independently, make the CLI print details.reason for parent_thread_invalid. No HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed.
1711.caveats: Worktree HEAD was a108fa7ef (origin/main, 5 commits past base 16ceb3a54); the relevant server/CLI/contract files are byte-identical at the base commit (verified via git diff), and origin/main does not fix the issue. The rejection is a deliberate design choice (kept explicitly in PR #235), so the issue is effectively a feature request; screenshots show behaviour with the guard experimentally removed (patch reverted afterwards), not the failing state, which is CLI-only text. Removing only the assertValidParentThread check would let a sandboxed parent spawn a full-permission child in another project because isLiveParentThread still requires same project.

1710.title: Archived threads cannot resume in the original chat
1710.rootCauseOneLine: Archiving the last live thread of a managed worktree retires the environment and, after the 5-minute grace window (PR #1016), the daemon runs `git worktree remove --force` and the environment becomes the terminal `destroyed` state; from there the app hides Unarchive/composer/handoff, unarchive only clears archivedAt (thread becomes live-but-unwritable, send -> 409 thread_environment_unavailable), fork is rejected, and no route/CLI can attach a new workspace to the thread — the deferred "continue from destroyed environment" path was never built.
1710.proposedFix: Server: add POST /threads/:id/restore-environment for threads whose managed-worktree environment is `destroyed` — create a new managed-worktree environment on the same host with baseBranch = old environment's branchName (the logic resolveForkEnvironment already has), updateThread({environmentId}) (DB layer supports it, emits environment-changed), let normal provisioning build the worktree, verify/fallback provider session resume with the new cwd. App/CLI/SDK: in the environment-gone banner add "Restore workspace from branch <b>" and "Continue in new thread" (handoff without reuseEnvironmentId), same in the "..." menu instead of a bare Unarchive that yields a zombie; add `bb thread restore-environment`; show the 5-minute deadline in the archived banner and rename "Environment archived" to "Workspace deleted". Cheap intermediate: allow fork (isolated mode) from a destroyed environment that still has branchName and expose it in the banner. Risks: branch deleted/merged (fall back to default base), uncommitted work is unrecoverable and must be stated, destroyed rows are pruned after 7 days so branchName must be captured earlier.
1710.caveats: This is a design gap rather than a crash: the behavior is deliberate ("Decision B*") and codified in tests; the unit repro test passes on main and documents the dead end. The Discord report itself was not accessible; the reporter may have been on <= v0.36.0 where destroy was immediate (no grace window) — the end state is identical. Committed work survives on the branch; only uncommitted changes and the ability to continue the conversation are lost. Worktree left with the added test file apps/server/test/public/issue-1710-archived-thread-dead-end.test.ts (worktree checked out at base 16ceb3a54, detached).

1681.title: Fix Pi process notification wake projection
1681.rootCauseOneLine: Pi extension-triggered turns (pi.sendMessage custom message with triggerTurn) emit role:"custom" message_start/message_end envelopes that bb's Pi translator classifies as provider/unhandled, and Pi's agent_end.messages contains that custom entry with string content which bb's piConversationMessageSchema (array-only) rejects, so agent_end becomes provider/unhandled and no turn/completed is ever emitted — the extension-started turn has no pi/prompt/settled fallback, so the thread stays 'Working…' forever with no input shown.

prReviews.topFinding: The string-content schema widening (the #1663 commit) correctly unsticks the turn, but the new item/completed userMessage projection is rendered by nothing in thread-view/app/CLI (verified live: bb thread log shows two consecutive 'ok' rows with no input), so 'process event is visible as turn input' is unmet; the 'no text response' warning path is dead because real Pi emits agent_start before the custom message_start (all new tests use the reversed order; probe test fails on the PR), and the fix keys on the third-party literal customType 'ad-process:notification' instead of role:'custom' generally.

1681.proposedFix: (1) Widen piConversationMessageSchema.content to z.union([z.string(), z.array(block)]) (as in #1663) — sufficient to emit turn/completed for extension-triggered turns; also JSON-round-trip raw events in toProviderRawEvent so unhandled payloads are not replaced by the serialization-error stub. (2) Handle message_start/message_end with role:'custom' generically in the Pi translator (project display:true custom messages as turn input when a bb turn is open, mark the rest as noise in visibility.ts) rather than matching customType 'ad-process:notification'. (3) Add a rendering path for provider-originated input: either project item/completed userMessage in @bb/thread-view (build-event-projection.ts + timeline/CLI formatters + snapshot test) as a user row with a non-user initiator, or emit an operation-style event that already renders. Tests must use the real order agent_start → message_start(custom). No HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed as ThreadEvent shapes are unchanged. Follow-up: idle provider-session reaping (30 min) disposes Pi sessions together with extension-owned background processes, which is a real 'never wakes' path.
1681.caveats: @aliou/pi-processes itself was not installed; the live repro uses a 30-line stand-in Pi extension sending the identical message shape (copied from pi-processes 0.10.9 source) via pi.sendMessage(..., {triggerTurn:true, deliverAs:'steer'}), run in a trusted scratch project via PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR pointing at a copy of ~/.pi/agent (bb's bridge has no Pi trust prompt, so project extensions are otherwise skipped silently). The worktree HEAD was a108fa7ef (5 commits past the brief's base); I checked out 16ceb3a54 for all main-branch work; none of the later origin/main commits touch the Pi translator, so the bug is not fixed on origin/main. The 30-minute idle-session-reaping concern was reasoned from code, not reproduced. 'Unhandled Pi event' rows are visible in dev builds because the server forces includeProviderUnhandledOperations in development; production only shows them with the setting enabled, so production users see just 'Working…' with no input/output.

1662.title: CLI/server payload drift: `bb plugin install <path>` gets HTTP 422 'expected {source}' while direct POST /api/v1/plugins/install succeeds
1662.rootCauseOneLine: Since fc3454809 (bb-app 0.38.0) the SDK/CLI always sends `selection: {kind:"root"}` in POST /api/v1/plugins/install, and every pre-0.38.0 server validates that body with a strict `{source}`-only zod schema, so a newer CLI against an older running server gets HTTP 422 'expected { "source": string }' while a bare `{"source":…}` curl passes; matched versions work in both directions except this one.
1662.proposedFix: (1) In packages/sdk/src/areas/plugins.ts make pluginSourceSelection return undefined for a root install and omit `selection` from the request body (server already defaults it); update the body assertions in packages/sdk/test/sdk.test.ts:1423, apps/app/src/hooks/queries/plugin-catalog-queries.test.ts:104 and AddPluginDialog.test.tsx:150,180 (patch prototyped and verified: repro test passes, SDK suite 92/92, typecheck clean, end-to-end request accepted by a 0.37.0 server). (2) Add a CLI-side version-skew check: read GET /api/v1/system/version currentVersion, compare with the CLI's resolveBbAppVersion(), and warn/fail with a clear 'CLI 0.38.0 vs server 0.37.0' message (skip for 0.0.0-dev) — needed because even with (1) the newer CLI then fails parsing the older server's response (required publisherLabel). (3) Rule of thumb: clients never send defaulted/optional fields they were not asked to set, so additive server changes stay forward-compatible with strict schemas.
1662.caveats: The reporter gave no versions; the exact CLI/server pair is inferred from the quoted error string (only emitted by pre-fc3454809 servers), the filing time (22h after 0.38.0 hit npm) and their fork context. Reproduced with real released artifacts (bb-app@0.38.0 CLI vs bb-app@0.37.0 server run on a scratch data dir) and a failing unit test at 16ceb3a54; with matched versions the command succeeds, so it is not reproducible on a single current build. Not fixed on origin/main a108fa7ef. Reproducing from inside a bb thread requires `unset BB_CLI` (the daemon-injected re-exec silently swaps the CLI). The worktree keeps only the new repro test file; the prototype fix was reverted and saved as a patch.

1656.title: Replies to mid-turn messages disappear from the timeline when the turn completes
1656.rootCauseOneLine: Completed-turn grouping (packages/thread-view/src/completed-turn-grouping.ts, rule from #897) splits a turn at user boundaries and keeps only each segment's LAST assistant/error message outside the "Worked for" fold, so the direct reply to a mid-turn steer (and answered AskUserQuestion cards, which are groupable and not boundaries) is folded once turn/completed arrives; the running view uses no grouping, hence the visible disappearance.

prReviews.topFinding: Regresses every ordinary follow-up turn: the initial user message of a tell-started turn sits inside turn.messages and arms preserveNextTerminalMessage, and the new final flushGroupedMessages(true) surfaces the penultimate message, so an unsteered turn goes from 'user, Worked for, final' to 'user, first reply, Worked for, penultimate, final' (verified on the real event log of thr_3qxpfum5zs and synthetic scenario A), contradicting the PR's own description; the final-flush change is built on the issue's refuted second bullet (turn terminal is already sliced out before grouping).

1656.proposedFix: Preferred: in groupCompletedTurnSummaryMessages emit every top-level assistant-text/error message (and answered user-question-lifecycle messages) as ungrouped rows in source order and fold only runs of tool/operation activity, so running and completed views agree (also fixes #1355); mind row-count/cache limits noted on closed PR #1508 and update CLI/app snapshot tests. Minimal alternative: keep #897's one-survivor rule but additionally preserve the first assistant/error message after a MID-turn user input only (steer, external boundary, answered question) — not the turn's initial user row — leave the final flush unchanged, make answered questions ungroupable boundaries, and add tests shaped like real follow-up turns (user message inside turn.messages) and spawn turns (outside).
1656.caveats: Behavior is by design per #897 (product limitation, not a coding slip); whether it is a bug is a product call. Issue Type/Effort project fields were not readable (token lacks read:project). AskUserQuestion folding was verified only at unit level, not with a live provider. The worktree branch had been moved to a108fa7ef before I started; I checked out 16ceb3a54 (detached) for all repro runs and verified the grouping files are identical between the two commits. Live repro required three attempts because claude-code tends to end the turn right after acknowledging a steer; the counting prompt in the report is the one that worked. 1654.title: claude login doesn't apply to exiting thread and requires restart

1558.title: bb-app can enroll a host against the wrong server after its server child fails with EADDRINUSE
1558.rootCauseOneLine: bb-app's waitForHealth() accepts any 200 from /health on the configured port (a constant {ok:true}) with no identity check, so a foreign bb server on the same port satisfies the probe on the first poll before the launcher's own server child dies with EADDRINUSE; the launcher then mints an enroll key from that foreign server and its daemon persists the resulting host key into the wrong data dir (before binding its own port), which the correct server later rejects with 401/INVALID_API_KEY.

A foreign server then never satisfies the probe, the child's EADDRINUSE exit surfaces as 'Process exited before becoming healthy', and maybeAddAutoJoinEnv/enrollment is never reached. Launcher-to-server only; no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. Also: server should log 'Server listening' only on the listening event and turn EADDRINUSE into a bb-authored fatal message; superviseFullStackProcesses should stop after N consecutive exit-before-listen restarts instead of looping '✓ Server restarted' forever; daemon's fatal 401/403 message can hint that <dataDir>/auth.json is unknown to <serverUrl> and can be removed to re-enroll (do not auto-delete).

1131.caveats: Absolute stall times were reproduced at ~10x smaller magnitude (0.28-0.46 s cold vs the reporter's 3.4 s) because this host has local NVMe and 16 cores; the transferable evidence is 77-100 MB of disk reads / 918 major page faults for a 1.7 MiB page and the query plans, not milliseconds. 1670.title: HEIC images aren't rendered in the UI
1670.rootCauseOneLine: bb stores and serves pasted HEIC bytes verbatim as a localImage (content-type image/heic) and renders the URL in a plain ; Chromium (web + Electron) has no HEIC decoder and bb never transcodes, so the thumbnail/timeline image is broken — and the provider (Codex) cannot process the image either.
1670.proposedFix: Transcode HEIC/HEIF once at the server upload boundary in storeAttachment (apps/server/src/services/projects/attachments.ts): detect image/heic|heif (or .heic/.heif extension), decode with a WASM libheif package (heic-decode/heic-convert; sharp's prebuilt libvips lacks HEIC), store JPEG (PNG if alpha), return mimeType image/jpeg + new path/sizeBytes, enforce the 10MB limit on output, 400 on decode failure. No wire/protocol change needed. Also render an "unsupported image" tile on onError in AttachmentPreview/ConversationAttachments. Regression test = the repro vitest (upload real HEIC -> served type must be Chromium-decodable).
1670.caveats: Repro run on Linux headless Chromium 145 (same Blink decoders as Electron); macOS Safari would likely render HEIC natively (not tested, no Apple hardware). Claude Code Read-tool behavior with HEIC inferred from code, not run. Worktree was initially at origin/main a108fa7ef; I checked out 16ceb3a54 before the live repro and confirmed the relevant files are identical between the two. Repro test file left uncommitted in the worktree at apps/server/test/public/repro-1670-heic-attachment.test.ts.

1603.title: Mobile Remote Access Template - UI/UX Hidden Due to Responsiveness Issues
1603.rootCauseOneLine: The home-route chunk (workspace-checkout-display, via @pierre/diffs + remark-gfm) cannot load on any Safari 16.x engine: regex lookbehind literals from @pierre/diffs and mdast-util-gfm-autolink-literal fail to parse on Safari 16.0-16.3, and on Safari 16.4-16.6 rolldown/Vite 8 constant-folds oniguruma-to-es's try/catch RegExp `v`-flag feature detection to `true`, so an unguarded `RegExp("[[^a]]","v")` throws at module top level; React lazy throws and AppErrorBoundary blanks the whole UI. Not a CSS/responsive bug.
1603.proposedFix: (1) Restore the bundler-folded feature detection: pnpm-patch oniguruma-to-es (and regex) so the `new RegExp("[[]]","v")` / `(?i:)` probes are opaque to rolldown (e.g. `Reflect.construct(globalThis.RegExp, [...])`), or exclude those modules from rolldown's pure-call elision, and report `new RegExp(...)`-is-not-pure upstream to rolldown; guard with a vitest that scans apps/app/dist/assets for `unicodeSets:!0`. This fixes iOS 16.4-16.7. (2) Either declare iOS 16.4+ the floor or pnpm-patch @pierre/diffs (SPLIT_WITH_NEWLINES lookbehind) and mdast-util-gfm-autolink-literal (email lookbehind) for iOS 16.0-16.3. (3) Add an ES5 inline feature probe in apps/app/index.html that shows a clear "bb needs iOS/Safari 17+" notice instead of loading the bundle, and make AppErrorBoundary recognise chunk SyntaxErrors as an unsupported-browser condition. (4) Add a CI WebKit smoke on the built app with a v-flag-rejecting init script to emulate the oldest supported Safari.

1545.title: Spawned agent shells inherit _VOLTA_TOOL_RECURSION, breaking bare node/npm/npx
1545.rootCauseOneLine: Volta stamps _VOLTA_TOOL_RECURSION=1 on the bb-app it launches; bb forwards it to the daemon and sanitizeInheritedChildProcessEnv (packages/process-utils/src/index.ts:188) only strips BB_*/NODE_ENV, while the daemon swaps PATH for the login-shell PATH that puts Volta's node/npm/npx shims back in front, so the shims see the guard, skip platform resolution and fail with "Node is not available" (also breaking $BB_CLI and bb, both #!/usr/bin/env node).
1545.proposedFix: Strip _VOLTA_TOOL_RECURSION in sanitizeInheritedChildProcessEnv (packages/process-utils/src/index.ts), the single choke point for every bb-spawned child (provider bridges, terminals, git, plugin hosts, script automations); one-hunk diff at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1545/repro/proposed-fix.diff. Mirrors Volta's own `volta run` (removes the same var because a new command is a new context). No wire change, no protocol bump. Verified: repro test flips from fail to pass and the same Claude Code turn prints v24.19.0 while the daemon still carries the guard. Optional hardening: also drop it in bb-app createDaemonEnv/createServerEnv.
1545.caveats: Reproduced on Linux with Volta 2.0.2 installed into a scratch VOLTA_HOME and a wrapper $SHELL so the daemon's login-shell PATH probe yields "Volta shims first, no other Node" (the reporter's mac/zsh setup is not available). The one simulated element is injecting _VOLTA_TOOL_RECURSION=1 into the dev instance's env instead of launching bb-app through a real Volta package shim; a real Volta package shim (probe package installed via `npm i -g` under Volta) was shown to set exactly that variable. The worktree HEAD had drifted to a108fa7ef at start; I pinned it to 16ceb3a54 before all repro runs (none of the 5 intervening commits touch the relevant files). 1440.rootCauseOneLine: apps/app/src/app.css sets no user-select policy at all, so every element keeps the browser default (auto) and sidebar labels, header, composer footer and hidden a11y labels all join drag selections and Ctrl/Cmd-A; only ad-hoc select-none on drag handles/menu items exists.

1304.title: Composer keystroke cost scales with the mounted timeline size
1304.rootCauseOneLine: ThreadDetailViewInternal subscribes to the composer draft store via usePromptDraftStorage (only to get the stable addQuote/storageKey), so every keystroke re-renders the whole 3k-line thread view; each render rebuilds threadOpenContext, which (identity-keyed memo in useLocalOpenTargets) churns openPathInFileTarget -> getLocalFileContextMenuItems -> the MarkdownLocalFileContextMenuContext.Provider value wrapping the timeline, forcing React to scan the entire mounted timeline subtree (1.5k fibers small, 17.9k fibers big) for consumers on every keystroke.
1304.proposedFix: Two-part diff (/tmp/bb-reports/issues/1304/repro/fix.diff, +54/-8, typecheck + 439 app tests pass): (A) extend getPromptDraftAccessor with storageKey + addQuote and make ThreadDetailView use useMemo(() => getPromptDraftAccessor(scope)) instead of usePromptDraftStorage, so the thread view no longer subscribes to per-keystroke draft writes; (B) in useLocalOpenTargets memoize openContext structurally on (kind, hostId, serverOrigin) instead of object identity so callers that rebuild an equal context per render get stable callbacks and the timeline-wide MarkdownLocalFileContextMenuContext value stops changing. Measured: rendered fibers/key 180 -> 81, propagateParentContextChanges 127 ms -> 3 ms per 71 keys, script time 20.0 -> 12.8 ms/key on the fully mounted 2.3k-event thread; big thread now types as fast as a 13-row thread.
1304.caveats: Timing numbers are from a dev build (StrictMode, jsxDEV) on a shared machine, so absolute ms/key vary +-5 ms between runs; the deterministic counters (render counts, changed-provider subtree sizes) and React's propagateParentContextChanges self time are the reliable signals. The unit repro test pins the two mechanisms at hook level (draft-store subscription; identity-keyed openContext memo) rather than rendering the real ThreadDetailView, which the app test suite only renders mocked. Seeded threads contain no markdown links, so the measured context-scan cost is the floor (real threads with file links would additionally re-render every MarkdownAnchor per keystroke). The issue's 94 ms long task was only sporadically matched (122/59 ms long tasks in base runs, none in fixed runs). Remaining ~20 ms/key is composer-local and out of scope. Worktree left with fix + test applied on top of 16ceb3a54 (branch bb/address-open-issues-and-prs-thr_j4hfucc5bb was ahead at a108fa7ef when I started; I checked out 16ceb3a54 detached).
